questions.q: Is Hartwell Logistics, the company in this case study, a real business?
options: No — it's explicitly described as a fictional, illustrative composite scenario
Yes — it is a real company whose name was changed for privacy
The lesson does not say whether it is real or fictional
Yes — it is a real, named freight company
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly labels Hartwell Logistics as fictional and illustrative, not a real company, consistent with this catalog's policy against presenting invented scenarios as real.

questions.q: What was the root problem at Hartwell Logistics, per this lesson?
options: The company had no database of any kind
Three teams each maintained their own definition of 'on-time delivery' with no shared standard, so the numbers never matched
The company had too many catalogs and needed to delete some
A single employee deleted all company data
questions.explain: Three competing informal definitions, with no governance tying them together, meant the executive report never matched any individual team's internal numbers.

questions.q: In the Chapter 2 step of the walkthrough, what made the new 'on-time delivery' definition usable, per this lesson?
options: It was written anonymously with no review at all
It avoided stating any specific threshold or time zone
It passed the four-part test from Lesson 7 and went through formal approval with an accountable steward
It was approved by the IT department rather than a business steward
questions.explain: The definition stated a specific, measurable rule (arrival by the promised date, in the destination time zone) and went through Lesson 8's approval workflow with Operations as the accountable steward.

questions.q: Why did ActualDeliveryTimestamp qualify for Chapter 4's elevated CDE documentation treatment, per this lesson?
options: It scored high on the CDE criteria because it directly feeds a metric reported to the board
CDE status was assigned randomly for this walkthrough
Every column in every database automatically qualifies as a CDE
It was the only column in the entire database
questions.explain: Feeding a board-reported metric is exactly the kind of regulatory/decision-impact criterion from Lesson 16 that justifies CDE-level rigor.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why did the final fix actually work three months later?
options: The company hired ten new data scientists
The executive report was discontinued entirely
All three spreadsheets were simply deleted with no replacement
There was now exactly one definition, one source system, and one place to look it up — not because anyone got better at math
questions.explain: The lesson's closing point is that giving one concept one home — not a math or skill improvement — was what actually resolved the recurring mismatch.
